title: Memory-recall 27.4% hit rate decomposed: intent-pollution fix alone caps the surface at ~36% best-case — floor math + corpus are the co-dominant miss cause; and 100% of recall benefit accrues to 'main' (zero sub-agent rows in 281), so the agent layer is fully memory-blind

evidence.quote:
Before starting implementation tasks, agents (kraken, architect, phoenix,
spark) should check the archival memory for relevant prior learnings.

telemetry: 281 rows; hit 27.4% (~77 hits); pollution 24.6% (69 rows); by_source empty 154 / db 127 (zero 'local' rows — corroborates D3b-03/06 dead local arm); p50 top_score=0; by_subagent: main 281/281
observe_how: Deterministic arithmetic on the harvest table: even if all 69 polluted rows are misses, best-case clean hit rate = 77/(281-69) = 36.3% — so intent sanitization alone recovers <=9pp of the 72.6% miss rate; the remaining ~135 clean-intent misses sit with the HYBRID_FLOOR math (D3b-01/08) and corpus coverage. p50 top_score=0 means the MEDIAN per-prompt recall surfaces nothing scoreable. Confirm post-fix by re-running the harvest split: hit rate among non-polluted rows vs polluted rows, and watch for any non-'main' by_subagent entry (today there are none, despite agent-memory-recall.md mandating agent recall).

title: Hook-coverage 'complete' claim is TypeScript-only: 9 git-tracked Python hooks in .claude/hooks/*.py were never inventoried and never subject-lined — including braintrust_hooks.py, registered LIVE on 5 events in repo + active + template

evidence.quote:
"""Braintrust tracing hooks - Cross-platform Python port.

Replaces the 5 bash hooks + common.sh:
- session_start

causal_links: Root-caused to harvest.mjs:36 — inventory-hooks.json is built from readdirSync('.claude/hooks/src').filter(f=>f.endsWith('.ts')), so the 111-hook denominator the GAP1 'complete' claim rests on is TypeScript-only by construction. The 5 braintrust_hooks.py registrations live in settings.json but not in srcBase (harvest.mjs:59), so the diff cannot see them.

Contradicts the GAP1 lead's framing that hooks are 'the one slice that is genuinely done' and its SUGGESTED action to WF-3 ('mark the hook-coverage axis CLOSED; no gap-fill agent needed for hooks'). Acting on that would leave a registered hot-path hook permanently un-reviewed.

D2g-03 already leaned on post_tool_use_tracker.py as the (dead-feed) writer behind pre-compact-continuity.ts's generateAutoSummary — i.e. a Python hook's behavior is load-bearing for a TS finding, yet the Python file itself carries no verdict.
observe_how: Independently reproduced the GAP1 completeness check: across all 15 D*.json coverage_manifests, all 111 TS hooks ARE the subject of >=1 coverage line (240 lines total; 0 TS hooks unaccounted) — so the TS claim holds. But `ls .claude/hooks/*.py` returns 9 git-tracked files (confirmed via `git ls-files`); a substring scan of every finding shows braintrust_hooks appears only in D2c coverage BODY text (never a subject line) and 6 of the 9 (post-tool-use-tracker [hyphen], auto-handoff-stop, hook_launcher, premortem-suggest, session_start_continuity, session-symbol-index) appear in NO finding at all. `grep` of repo settings.json confirms braintrust_hooks.py is bound to 5 events (user_prompt_submit/session_start/session_end/stop/post_tool_use); the active ~/.claude/settings.json mirrors all 5; the template registers all 5. braintrust_hooks.py is 33,982 bytes and makes httpx network calls per event (hot path).
telemetry: harvest.mjs's registrations-diff.json reports `registered_active_but_no_src: []` — falsely reassuring, because the no-src check is computed only over the TS srcBase and structurally cannot flag a registered .py command as un-sourced or un-reviewed. The only honest 'covered?' signal for Python hooks is absence from every coverage_manifest, which is what this finding measures.

title: daemon-client Windows TCP path double-shells the same model-controlled Grep pattern: query JSON (containing `pattern`) is interpolated into a PowerShell command, which is then wrapped in an execSync cmd.exe string (`powershell -Command "..."`). Inner PS escape covers ' only; outer cmd.exe escape covers " only — % & ^ < > | reach cmd.exe live.
causal_links: same model-controlled pattern as GAP4-01 (smart-search-router queryDaemonSync({cmd:'search',pattern}))
D5a flagged daemon-client.ts:582/589 as 'connInfo.path/psCommand, not user content' — that triage missed that `input` = JSON.stringify(query) carries the model's search `pattern`
telemetry: On Windows with the TLDR daemon reachable over TCP (connInfo.type==='tcp'), issue a Grep whose pattern contains a cmd.exe metachar (% ^ & < > |) and check for an injected effect through the outer `powershell -Command "..."` cmd.exe wrapper. The inner PS layer escapes ' -> '' (correct for PS), but the outer execSync only does psCommand.replace(/"/g,'\\"'); cmd.exe metachars in the pattern are untouched at the outer layer.
observe_how: smart-search-router.ts:76 calls queryDaemonSync({ cmd: 'search', pattern }, projectDir) with the model's Grep pattern. In daemon-client.ts queryDaemonSync (line 544) sets input = JSON.stringify(query) (line 565) — the pattern is now inside `input`. On the Windows branch (connInfo.type==='tcp'), input is interpolated into psCommand via `$writer.WriteLine('${input.replace(/'/g, "''")}')` (line 575), and the whole psCommand is run via execSync(`powershell -Command "${psCommand.replace(/"/g,'\\"')}"`) (line 582). Two shells, two escape regexes, neither covering the cmd.exe metacharacter set the OUTER layer is exposed to. A pattern containing %FOO% / & / ^ / > is interpreted by the outer cmd.exe. Remediation: pass the daemon payload over a real socket (net.Socket) or via spawnSync('powershell', ['-Command', psScript], {shell:false}) so no cmd.exe wrap and no string interpolation of `input` into a -Command argument.

evidence.quote: const response = queryDaemonSync({ cmd: 'search', pattern }, projectDir);
